heroText: Canmore works best as a base in Canada when you anchor days around Three Sisters, Grassi Lakes and Canmore Nordic Centre. Use those sights to understand the city's history, street life and visitor rhythm. Calgary International Airport (YYC) handles the main arrival flow, so hotel choice should balance the centre, transfer time and day-trip plans.

history.text: Canmore was officially named in 1884 by Canadian Pacific Railway director Donald A. Smith (later 1st Baron Strathcona and Mount Royal).
In 1886, Queen Victoria granted a coal mining charter to the town, and the No. 1 mine was opened in 1887.
The Canmore Hotel was built in 1890 on the main street.

history.label: 1890s
history.text: By the 1890s, a North-West Mounted Police barrack had been instated on Main Street, however, it was vacated in 1927.

history.label: 20th century
history.text: The coal mining industry in Canmore boomed well into the 20th century.
In 1965, with a population of 2,000, Canmore was incorporated as a town.

history.label: 1970s
history.text: By the 1970s, the market for coal was diminished, and in 1979 Canmore Mines Ltd. ceased operations.

history.label: 1980s
history.text: Canmore's economic future seemed dismal until the announcement in the early 1980s that Calgary would be hosting the 1988 Winter Olympics, and that Canmore would play host to the Nordic events.
